transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Catalyst - Procurement), Daniel Owens (Catalyst - Legal), Marta Ruiz (Catalyst - CTO)

Summary (auto):
Quick procurement/legal review focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets for Dedicated vs Hosted, and final pricing approval steps. Agreement to circulate redline and SOC2 docs, follow-up technical onboarding scheduled.

Topics: MSA/DPA redline, SOC 2, SLAs (latency/uptime), pricing (reserved capacity), vendor onboarding checklist, data residency/KMS, support SLAs

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:08] Sofia Martinez: All right, hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. I see we've got Priya, Daniel, Marta — thanks. Quick run through agenda, procurement and legal items, then pricing and next steps.
[00:00:22] Priya Shah: Yep thanks Sofia, appreciate it. We got legal on the line today, uh Daniel, who will lead on the DPA questions. Marta is here for technical constraints.
[00:00:31] Daniel Owens: Hi all. We'll try to be concise, main things are data residency, audit rights, and indemnity language.
[00:00:38] Ethan Zhao: Great — I'll jump in on the technical coverage and SLAs. Quick note: Redwood's SOC 2 is available, we have a DPA template, and for Dedicated customers we offer VPC/private options.
[00:00:50] Marta Ruiz: For us, two constraints: 1) we need AES-256 at rest with KMS integration, and 2) ability to retain logs for 12 months for audit. Also latency SLOs are important — we run real-time underwriting flows.
[00:01:12] Sofia Martinez: Noted. On the KMS side, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS/HSM for Private. For Hosted customers we can integrate with customer KMS in many cases — we'll send the specific patterns.
[00:01:28] Daniel Owens: On the DPA, switching the data processing clauses to our spec — we usually ask for broad subprocessor notification and 30-day notice for changes. Is that standard?
[00:01:41] Ethan Zhao: Typical for enterprise customers, yes. Our DPA has a subprocessors section; we can agree to notification and reasonable prior notice. We may need to check specific legal terms around liability caps in the MSA.
[00:01:55] Priya Shah: Liability cap is one of the sticking points for procurement — we have thresholds depending on the service tier. Also need clarity on SLA credits and remedies.
[00:02:06] Sofia Martinez: Understood. For Redwood Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets — I'll let Ethan share the numbers.
[00:02:14] Ethan Zhao: Sure. For Dedicated we target 99.95% uptime for the serving control plane and a p95 generation latency target that depends on model & config — but typical under mid-100s ms for short prompts. For hosted we present benchmark numbers by model. Keep in mind quantization and batching affect cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:02:34] Marta Ruiz: When you say p95 mid-100s, is that single-token latency or full request? Our underwriting prompts can be 1k tokens.
[00:02:44] Ethan Zhao: Good call — that's end-to-end token latency under common prompt sizes; for 1k tokens you should expect higher per-request time, but we can provide profiling. Also auto-prefix caching and KV cache reduces cost for repeated contexts.
[00:02:58] Daniel Owens: Can you confirm data residency — our policy requires data stored in US-only for now.
[00:03:05] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely — we can pin region and restrict storage to US regions in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we'll need to confirm whether region pinning is available per account; in many cases yes, with enterprise account. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[00:03:20] Priya Shah: Great. Okay legal redlines — we'll send a clean mark-up, but do we have a standard position on indemnities?
[00:03:28] Daniel Owens: We usually ask for mutual indemnity except for IP claims, and carveouts for gross negligence.
[00:03:34] Sofia Martinez: Our standard MSA is mutual indemnification with a cap tied to subscription fees; however, we can escalate for enterprise deals. We'll flag the legal team if you need a modified cap.
[00:03:47] Priya Shah: Pricing — our procurement council needs committed pricing tiers for reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go. Sofia, you had mentioned a worksheet?
[00:03:56] Sofia Martinez: Yes, I'll share a pricing worksheet that shows per-token rates for hosted, and reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated with monthly commit tiers and burst options. There will be a separate column with estimated unit economics as you scale.
[00:04:10] Marta Ruiz: Also need to understand how autoscaling works — we can't accept surprising bursts that cause latency degradation for critical flows.
[00:04:19] Ethan Zhao: On Dedicated you configure autoscale policy with guaranteed baseline capacity and burst pool. We can set throttling and fallback policies. Also model variants for fallback — cheaper quantized variant in a different pool.
[00:04:31] Priya Shah: Any compliance docs we should expect? SOC2, pen test reports, maybe ISO overview?
[00:04:37] Sofia Martinez: SOC 2 Type II report, attack surface summary, and SOC 3/ISO snippets where available. We'll attach those.
[00:04:43] Daniel Owens: On subprocessor list — how often do you update and how is that communicated?
[00:04:48] Ethan Zhao: Quarterly updates; we notify customers before changes and publish the list in the console.
[00:04:53] [00:05:02] Sofia Martinez: Quick pause — are there any hard deal timelines?
[00:05:05] Priya Shah: Procurement committee meets 2025-11-20. If we can get pricing and redlines by 11-15, we can fast-track for approval.
[00:05:13] Marta Ruiz: From infra, we need an onboarding window in the week of 11-24 to run benchmarks and a short POC.
[00:05:20] Sofia Martinez: Perfect — we'll align that.
[00:05:24] Daniel Owens: A few DPA-specific asks: additional audit rights paragraph, clarification on deletion timelines when contract terminates, and explicit KMS key destruction process.
[00:05:36] Ethan Zhao: Deletion timelines depend on deployment mode; for Private/Dedicated we can do customer-managed lifecycle. For Hosted we offer secure deletion within agreed window — we'll capture in the DPA redline.
[00:05:48] Priya Shah: Also, do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning?
[00:05:53] Sofia Martinez: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for provisioning; we'll send the integration guide.
[00:05:59] Marta Ruiz: For the technical onboarding, can we get a pre-call with infra to share network diagrams and ports? We use strict egress rules.
[00:06:07] Ethan Zhao: Absolutely — SE-led network runbook call, we'll include that in the onboarding invite.
[00:06:12] [00:06:40] (brief cross-talk while calendar invites are checked)
[00:06:42] Sofia Martinez: Moving on — sample clause questions. Daniel, you mentioned liability caps — any initial numbers?
[00:06:49] Daniel Owens: We usually see a tiered cap — often 6-12 months of fees for SaaS; for critical systems we ask higher. We'll propose language.
[00:06:58] Sofia Martinez: Ok we'll flag for legal escalation.
[00:07:05] Priya Shah: On support SLAs — we need 24/7 incident support for critical outages and a named escalation path.
[00:07:13] Ethan Zhao: Enterprise customers can opt into an enhanced support package: 24/7 P1 response, dedicated CSM, and on-call engineering. We'll detail the runbook and on-call SLA in the support addendum.
[00:07:25] Marta Ruiz: And does that include runbook rehearsal or DR playbooks?
[00:07:29] Ethan Zhao: Yes, add-on professional services can include DR exercises and runbook reviews.
[00:07:33] Priya Shah: Great. Any blockers on our side with the redline process?
[00:07:38] Daniel Owens: We'll send a clean redline by end of day 11-13, but we'll need Redwood to respond in 48 hours ideally.
[00:07:45] Sofia Martinez: We'll aim to respond faster — Ethan and I will triage with legal and compliance.
[00:07:49] [00:07:55] (background noise, someone joining late)
[00:08:01] Sofia Martinez: Quick technical note on data flows: Redwood's control plane stores metadata; customer data can be configured to remain in customer-managed buckets for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, by default we store ephemeral tensors and can enable customer storage integration.
[00:08:20] Marta Ruiz: We want logs in our SIEM — do you support log forwarding or syslog?
[00:08:25] Ethan Zhao: Yes, log forwarding to customer SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export; retention and schema are configurable.
[00:08:33] Priya Shah: Ok let's talk pricing scenarios briefly — Sofia, can you outline a mid-size commit?
[00:08:40] Sofia Martinez: Sure: example — 2m tokens/month reserved with Dedicated baseline yields X per-token effective rate, plus a burst pool for spikes. We'll put numbers in the worksheet; there are also committed discounts for longer terms.
[00:08:54] Marta Ruiz: For benchmarking, can you provide a profile of expected throughput per GPU and the recommended instance types?
[00:09:01] Ethan Zhao: Yes, we'll include a throughput matrix and recommended infra for the models you plan to use. For heavy token workloads, we usually recommend models with KV optimizations and quantized runtime to balance cost.
[00:09:13] Daniel Owens: Any vendor onboarding docs we should expect?
[00:09:17] Sofia Martinez: We'll send a vendor onboarding packet — includes MSA/DPA, compliance docs, onboarding checklist, network runbook, and a proposed project plan for the POC.
[00:09:27] Priya Shah: That should be fine.
[00:09:30] [00:10:12] (brief pause, participants checking calendar)
[00:10:15] Sofia Martinez: Let's recap next steps before we wrap: Ethan to send SOC2 and DPA redline, Sofia to send pricing worksheet, Redwood to schedule technical onboarding week of 11-24. Any other asks?
[00:10:30] Priya Shah: Please include a sample SAML setup doc and SCIM mapping for users.
[00:10:34] Marta Ruiz: Include network ports and egress addresses for our firewall team.
[00:10:38] Daniel Owens: And please call out subprocessors and notification cadence in the DPA.
[00:10:44] Sofia Martinez: Will do.
[00:10:50] Priya Shah: Timeline again — procurement meets 11-20 and expects deliverables by 11-15. We can give you a soft yes if all looks good.
[00:10:58] Sofia Martinez: Great, we'll be aggressive on timing.
[00:11:05] [00:11:22] (wrap-up smalltalk)
[00:11:30] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with an email summarizing the redlines and attachments.
[00:11:35] Ethan Zhao: I'll draft the technical agenda for the onboarding call.
[00:11:40] Priya Shah: Thanks all.
[00:11:45] Daniel Owens: Thanks.
[00:11:47] Marta Ruiz: Bye.

--- End of call notes (transcript trimmed for clarity) ---
